newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds off in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds off in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities slipped into negative territory with Treasuries during a quiet Friday afternoon trading session, traders said.
Pass-through securities fell in line with Treasuries after data on early November consumer sentiment weighted prices down, said one regional trader.
The University of Michagan's preliminary November measure of consumer sentiment rose to 98.9 against 96.5 in October.
"Its been relatively quiet today and trading behavior has been typical," the trader said, adding that yield spreads over Treasuries "narrow on downticks and widen a little on upticks."
No major bid lists were cited Friday, traders said.
"Its been very quiet today," echoed a New York-based trader.
"There was about a $1.0 billion bid list yesterday in a variety of (mortgaged-backed) products ... but nothing going on today," he said.
By late Friday, pass-throughs nearly matched Treasuries' losses, with 30-year paper falling 4/32 to 6/32 in coupons of 8.0 percent and smaller.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were off 4/32 at 100-29/32, yielding 122 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper were off 4/32 as well, at 100-22/32 and 100-28/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was down 7/32 at 102-11/32 to yield 6.18 percent.
